style.summary:
style of A: A is casual and repetitive, with Yeah yeah and just repeated.
style of B: B is hesitant with stammers, but commits decisively with I will send him an email.

A: A's casual tone keeps the exchange friendly, which makes A's suggestions easy to adopt.
A's repetition of just reinforces A's point until it sounds settled.
A's Yeah yeah signals agreement that creates an appearance of consensus.
B: B's decisive I will send him an email shows B's commitment in a way A's stance does not.
B's hesitation does not prevent B from setting the next step.
B's directness in stating the plan gives B authority over the action.

A: A's casual tone gives no direction, so B's decisive plan is what the group follows.
A's repetition is circular and does not force B to change the plan.
A's agreement is about the plan B proposed, so consensus is built on B's proposal.
B: B's commitment is a single email, while A's call for contact is the broader and more durable step.
B's hesitation weakens the authority of the plan, which A can reshape.
B's directness is limited to one action, so A's broader suggestion matters more.

content.summary:
content of A: A's content is a general call for more contact between the parties.
content of B: B's content is a description of a different method and a concrete plan to email.

A: A's call for more contact shapes the subject of the exchange toward the relationship.
A's focus on the fact that the parties are connected sets the substance A cares about.
A's suggestion of greater contact defines what the parties should do next.
B: B's description of a different method supplies technical substance.
B's plan to tell him exactly what we are doing gives B control of the account.
B's identification of what they were trying to do sets the facts the group discusses.

A: A's call for contact is a general remark, and B's email is the concrete substance that will actually happen.
A's focus on connection is vague, so B's method sets the real content.
A's suggestion can be replaced by B's plan, so B determines what the parties do next.
B: B's email is a unilateral step, and A's call for more contact is what makes the relationship work, so A has the broader influence.
B's method is described briefly, so A can treat it as a detail.
B's account is a promise A can hold B to, so the control rests with A.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: A interrupts with I mean - and resumes after B's Um.
coordination of B: B takes the floor and then yields with Um and Mm-hmm.

A: A's interruption with I mean takes the floor when B pauses.
A resumes the thread after B's hesitation, which shows A controls the flow.
A's repeated attempts to speak keep A in the position of initiating topics.
B: B takes the floor for the substantive turn and sets the topic.
B's yielding with Um and Mm-hmm shows B decides when A may take over.
B's closing of the plan gives B the last word on the action.

A: A's interruption is cut off by B's Um, so the floor remains with B.
A's resumption follows B's yield, so the sequence still belongs to B.
A's attempts to speak are short, so B's initiatives set the topics.
B: B's floor is limited by A's interruptions, so B does not fully control the turns.
B's yield gives no real control, since A keeps speaking.
B's last word is answered by A's call for contact, so the final word is shared.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: A shows engagement with a suggestion to be in contact more.
engagement of B: B shows engagement with a concrete action.

A: A's suggestion for more contact shows A cares about the relationship.
A's repeated interjections show A is actively trying to contribute.
A's suggestion keeps A central to the wider outcome.
B: B's concrete action shows B is taking responsibility.
B's admission of not knowing shows honest involvement.
B's plan to tell him exactly shows B is invested in clarity.

A: A's suggestion is general, and B's concrete action is the engagement that moves things forward.
A's interjections are not completed, so the contribution is limited.
A's central role depends on B's plan being accepted.
B: B's admission of not knowing weakens the claim to knowledge, so A's suggestion is the better guide.
B's engagement is limited to one email, while A's suggestion is broader.
B's promise of clarity can be checked by A, so B's investment is accountable to A.
